summary.text: Chedrick Greene is the Democratic state senator for Michigan's District 35, who won a May 5, 2026 special general election and is on the November 3, 2026 ballot seeking a full term.
A U.S. Marine Corps veteran and Saginaw fire captain, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that his priorities include making life more affordable and bringing better-paying jobs to the region.

paragraphs.text: Chedrick Greene was born in Saginaw, Michigan, and graduated from Bridgeport High School in 1993.
He served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1994 to 2024.
His career experience includes working as a fire captain with the City of Saginaw Fire Department and as a district assistant to former state Senator Kristen McDonald Rivet.

Greene won the Democratic primary in February 2026 and the special general election on May 5, 2026, defeating Republican Jason Tunney and Libertarian Ali Sledz, and he took office on May 21, 2026, succeeding McDonald Rivet.
He advanced from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary and faces Tunney and Laurie Atwood of the U.S. Taxpayers Party in the general election.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Greene described himself as a 30-year Marine veteran, 26-plus-year firefighter and 31-plus-year union member and said he is passionate about pro-labor and pro-working-family policies.
He said his top priority is to make life more affordable and the region more attractive for better-paying jobs, and that he would work to expand education and skills training.
